To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proton finite-size correction to muonic-hydrogen 2P^{2}_{3/12} to 2s^{1}_{1/12} Lamb shift depends on the shape of proton form-factor only through its rms radius and (2) the correction is independent of the proton charge distribution.

the perturbation-theoretic finite-size correction for this transition, which is the subject of this thesis, is insensitive to the shape of the form-factor and is consistent with the value obtained by Pohl et. al.

the finite-size correction of 0.3 kHz to the 2P_{3/2} - 2S_{1/2} energy interval in muonic hydrogen, calculated with the experimental proton form-factor, differs by less than 0.01 kHz from the corresponding correction calculated with an electrically neutral, point-like proton.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the finite-size correction is not a sensitive measure of the proton charge-distribution and that a discrepancy of 4.9 sigmas is not warranted.

a more accurate analysis of the experimental data is required in order to confirm the CODATA value of the proton charge radius, and that this analysis must include the effects of higher-order perturbative and nonperturbative QED corrections.
